subject.title: fix(slack): keep health probes within their timeout

question: Should Slack health diagnostics deliberately fail on the first transient transport error or HTTP 429 so the probe always returns within its shared deadline, rather than spending that budget on Slack retries or Retry-After waiting?
rationale: The implementation is technically narrow and its live proof is strong, but the change intentionally selects an operational availability policy for existing Slack diagnostics that automated review cannot choose on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Adopt deadline-first probe semantics
options.body: Keep zero retries and immediate HTTP-429 rejection for the dedicated health-probe client, while leaving normal Slack reads and mutations on their existing policies.

options.title: Preserve retry behavior
options.body: Pause this PR and define a different probe policy if transient-retry visibility is more important than returning within the configured health deadline.

recommendation.title: Adopt deadline-first probe semantics
recommendation.body: Keep zero retries and immediate HTTP-429 rejection for the dedicated health-probe client, while leaving normal Slack reads and mutations on their existing policies.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent merged Slack read-client architecture and the current PR history identify this contributor as the closest available owner for the policy boundary.
